evidence.baseline: Part I has been the floor of the book ... Read what follows as the description of a substrate. The technologies humanity actually needs will grow from it, or they will not grow at all.

findings.diagnosis: The page contains six sentence fragments in a row naming what Part II will describe, three anaphoric It cannot sentences, and an unhedged closing binary. Every one of those is a construction the pass removed elsewhere in the volume. That it survived here intact is worth recording, because it shows the pass was not applying a rule consistently. It was making local judgments, and the same construction was kept on one page and deleted on the next.

regenerationTest.purpose: The rules must reproduce the section from the baseline without consulting the stored text.
regenerationTest.method: Byte comparison against the immutable baseline, then a read of the page against editorial/method/standard.md and both voice cards.
regenerationTest.conclusion: No new rule required, and no change made. The page is useful as a control. It carries the same constructions the pass deleted from the chapters on either side of it, and it carries no prohibited punctuation. The correlation is worth noting for the remaining sections: the pass appears to have rewritten most heavily where a mark had to be removed anyway, which is how a punctuation repair turns into a rebuild.
